# 0013 — Three kinds of notice, one of them spoken, and one registry of keys

**Date:** 2026-10-14 · **Status:** accepted

## Context

The 2026-10-14 audit asked for three shell-level pieces: a notification centre, because a toast is
ephemeral and capped at three, so the one that said "Re-index failed" during a meeting was gone; a
banner, because nothing could say "maintenance tonight" to the whole application; and a shortcut
registry, because `Kbd`, `MenuItem shortcut`, `Tooltip shortcut` and the palette's item hints all
printed keys that nothing guaranteed were bound, and `useCommandShortcut` was the only binding in the
system.

Each piece is easy on its own. Together they raise two questions the system had not answered:
which notice is for what, and who speaks. The audit had praised the existing restraint (the toast
region is the one polite live region a page has, `danger` is the only assertive toast, the palette
debounces its count), and three new surfaces that each announce would undo it.

## Decision

**Where a message goes depends on what it is about and how long it is true.**

| Notice | About | True for | Spoken |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Banner | the whole application | as long as the condition holds | no; once, politely, with `announce`, only when it appears mid-session |
| Callout | one page or region | as long as the condition holds | no |
| Toast | something that just happened | a few seconds | yes: the one polite region, assertive for `danger` |
| Notification centre | the record of what happened | until read | never |

The same event usually goes to a toast and to the centre: the toast says it now, the centre keeps
it. The centre has no live region and its unread count changes silently, because the toast already
announced the event; the count is in the bell's accessible name, heard when someone goes to the
bell. A banner present at page load is content, read in order after the skip link, in a landmark
named "Announcement".

**The words follow.** "Notification" is an event, in both the toast region (Base UI names it
"Notifications") and the centre. "Announcement" is a standing condition of the app. The content
page's table of words that are easy to swap records both, and "Mark all as read", which is not
Clear or Dismiss because nothing leaves the list.

**One registry of keys.** `useHotkeys(keys, handler, { label, group })` binds a shortcut and
registers its words with the nearest `HotkeysProvider`; `ShortcutsDialog` lists that registry and
nothing else, so a listed shortcut is always a bound one, printed from the string the listener
matches. `label` is required: a shortcut nobody can find is a shortcut nobody has. A key something
else binds (Base UI's F6 for the toast region) is listed with a `null` handler, not bound twice.
`useCommandShortcut` and the palette's new `CommandItem.hotkey` are `useHotkeys` underneath.

**`mod` follows the platform.** `mod` is ⌘ on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere, and only that.
`useCommandShortcut` used to accept both on every platform; on a Mac, Ctrl-K deletes to the end of
the line in every native text field, and on Windows ⌘ is the Windows key. Accepting both was the
hijack the registry exists to prevent.

**Typing is never hijacked.** A plain-key shortcut does not fire in a text field, a select, a
contenteditable region or a textbox widget; nothing fires during IME composition (`isComposing`, or
keyCode 229); key repeat and events a component already handled are ignored. A chord with ⌘ or
Ctrl does fire from a field, because it types nothing: that is how ⌘K reaches the palette from a
search box.

## Consequences

- On a Mac, Ctrl-K no longer opens the command palette, and on Windows and Linux ⌘K no longer does.
  Each platform's own chord still does.
- A page that wants its shortcuts listed mounts `HotkeysProvider` around `ToastProvider`. Without
  it, shortcuts still work and are simply unlisted.
- The banner's foot edge is the `--bar-w` status edge (`bar-bottom-*`) and it sits at `--z-sticky`,
  the app bar's step, from the edge and stacking tokens of 0.7.0.
- A fourth notice surface needs an answer to the "spoken" column before it ships.
